gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Creative's own US page rates the $66.49 Pebble Pro at 10 W RMS from a PC's USB-C port, and that it needs a separately sold 30 W USB PD adapter to reach 30 W RMS. The $94.99 Creative T60 gives 30 W RMS from its included AC power, and all three Creative picks (Pebble Pro, T60, Pebble X Plus) list SBC as their only Bluetooth codec.
standout_why: I could read only one of the cited rival pages. Stack and Value (2026-10-24) says the Pebble Pro's higher output needs a 30 W PD adapter sold separately, but it gives no RMS figures for USB power versus adapter power and does not mention codecs or latency. Its prices are Amazon prices from 2026-10-24 (Pebble Pro $64.99, Z407 $115.99, R1280DBs $159.99), and they no longer match the maker stores. The other cited pages (TechRadar, Tom's Guide, Tom's Hardware, PC Gamer) returned only their titles (111 characters) to WebFetch, and running curl or Python needed approval, which I didn't get. So I could not confirm that those four pages leave the 10 W versus 30 W RMS split out, and the score assumes they do.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's choice of the Pebble Pro as the cheapest pick, but only if the shopper accepts 10 W RMS from a PC's USB-C port or buys a 30 W PD adapter. Without the adapter, the T60 at $94.99 gives three times the RMS power for $28.50 more and needs no extra purchase. Edifier sells the G2000 II for $129.99, not the $109.99 on ChatGPT's card. $109.99 is the price of the original G2000, so that card mixes up two models.
